settings.selection_rationale: best available model. User selected Buchary (1999) mid-1970s Java Sea after proportional normalization of Macrozoobenthos diet0.660 to1 and computational BA completion for all28 groups. Printed source preserved separately; completed BA is not measured biomass change. TE WARN: near-zero Marine mammals transfer efficiency; retain method-specific limits.

settings.npp_policy: Annual observed support; unsupported years stay blank; no earliest-year proxy by default

groups.taxon_descr: Comprised of particulate and dissolved organic matters

Comprised of resident dolphins viz., Bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops spp), Spinner dolphins (Stenella longirostris), Irrawady dolphins (Orcaella brevirostris), Finless porpoises (Neophocaena phocaenoides), and Indo-Pacific Hump-backed dolphins (Sousa chinensis); and transient whales, viz., Sperm whales (Physeter catodon), Bryde's whales (Balaenoptera edenii), and Minke whales (B. acutorostrata)
Ariidae (Arius thalassinus), Carcharhinidae, Muraenesocidae, Serranidae (Epinephelus lanceolatus), Sphyrnidae, Stegostomidae, Pristidae, Rhinidae, and Rhinobatidae
Chirocentridae, large Scombridae, and Trichiuridae
Dasyatidae and Myliobatidae
Juveniles of the families Ariidae (Arius thalassinus), Carcharhinidae, Muraenesocidae, Serranidae (Epinephelus lanceolatus), Sphyrnidae, Stegostomidae, Pristidae, Rhinidae, and Rhinobatidae
Haemulidae, Lutjanidae (Pristipomoides typus), Muraenesocidae (Congresox talabon), Nomeidae, Psettodidae, Rachycentridae, Scatophagidae, Serranidae, and Mugilidae

Apogonidae, Ariidae, Ariommatidae, Caesionidae, Cynoglossidae, Dactylopteridae, Drepanidae, Ephippidae, Gerridae, Haemulidae, Holocentridae, Kurtidae, Menidae, Mullidae, Nemipteridae, Priacanthidae, Serranidae, Siganidae, Sillaginidae, Stromateidae, Synodontidae, Teraponidae and Sciaenidae
Clupeidae and Engraulidae
Rastrelliger brachysoma and R. kanagurta
Decapterus macrosoma, D. maruadsi and D. russelli
Includes squids (Loligo spp.), cuttlefish (Sepia spp.) and octopus (Octopus spp.)
Portunidae, Palinuridae, Scyllaridae, etc.
Gazza minuta, Leiognathus spp., and Secutor spp.
Belonidae, Carangidae, Harpodontidae, Hemirhamphidae, Lactaridae, Mobulidae, Sciaenidae (Kathala axillaris), and Scombridae (Auxis sp.)
Includes all adult shrimps, but data refer only to Penaeus spp. and Metapenaeus spp.
Juveniles of the families Chirocentridae, large Scombridae, and Trichiuridae
This group includes all juvenile shrimps, not just penaeid shrimps. However, the parameterization of this group is based on the juveniles of Penaeus spp. and Metapenaeus spp.

This functional group comprised of all biogenic organisms that live on and/or are attached to the sea floor, such as sponges (notably giant cup sponges, viz. Poterion nautilus, P. neptuni and P. amphitritae), gorgonians (sea fans and sea whips), soft corals, sea pens, sea anemones, etc.
This group includes all larger (size > 1.0 mm) mollusks and echinoderms, such as conch, oyster, scallops, clams, cockles, mussels, sea urchins, sea cucumbers, and sea stars

This group is designed to include all biota (notably fish) that ecologically depend (directly and/or indirectly) on living bottom structure (LBS, see components of group #10) to complete their life cycle. For this model, it includes fish of the families Balistidae, demersal Carangidae, Lethrinidae, Lutjanidae, Pentapodidae, Platacidae, Polynemidae, Sparidae, Sphyraenidae, Scaridae, Acanthuridae, and Tetraodontidae
Includes all burrowing benthos of the size < 1.0 mm, viz., polychaetes, mollusks, echinoderms, crustaceans, sipunculans, and benthic stage larvae of other larger organisms
All medusoid form of cnidarians (hydrozoa and scyphozoa only); however, scyphozoan medusae dominates
Chaetognaths (Sagitta spp.), annelids and ichthyoplankton
Mysids, sergestids, euphausiids, amphipodes, luciferidae, and other decapod larvae
Copepodes, ostracodes, bivalve larvae, cirripedia larvae, cladocerans, echinoderm larvae, larvacea, other mollusk larvae, and larvacea

Dominated by diatoms (Bacteriastrum sp., Biddulphia sp., Bacillaria sp., Chaetoceros sp., Coscinodiscus sp., Ditylum sp., Eucampia sp., Hemiaulus sp., Hemidiscus sp., Lauderia sp., Leptocylindricus sp., Nitzschia sp., Rhizosolenia sp., Skeletonema sp., Streptotheca sp., Thalassiothrix sp./Thalassionema sp.) and dinoflagellates (Ceratium sp., Dinophysis sp., and Peridinium sp.)
Marine algae (epilithic algae, endolithic algae, reef turf algae, benthic fleshy algae, macroalgae, and benthic algae) and spermatophytes (sea grass)
